headline: Europe holds near its record as the oil spike fades
tone: The overnight scare held in rates and the dollar, not in European stocks; the morning oil bid has faded.
body: Europe shrugged off the Nvidia shock: the STOXX 600 is up 0.1% at 664.75, close to the record high it set on Thursday, with the DAX up 0.2% and the FTSE 100 up 0.3%. Asia took it harder, with the Hang Seng down 1.5% while the Nikkei rose 0.5%.

The oil spike faded: Brent is back to $95.75, flat on the day after trading near $96.5 at 08:00, and WTI is down 0.6% at $88.21. The IEA's monthly report pointed to signs of the oil market rebalancing.

The rates scare is still in the price: the US 10-year closed Thursday at 5.10%, up 12bp, and the dollar is firm, with EUR/USD down 0.4% at 1.105 and USD/CHF up 0.7% at 0.838. The Bund is calmer at 3.36%.

The European morning data was soft rather than alarming: euro-area GDP grew 0.4% in the third quarter, down from 0.6%. Richemont fell about 6% in Zurich after slower jewellery growth, pulling the SMI down 0.2%.

views.text: Into the oil majors and out of renewables and miners. Shell is up 1.2%, TotalEnergies 1.4% and Equinor 1.3%, while Acciona Energía fell 5.7%, Grenergy 4.8% and Eolus 4.1%; Orrön is down 2.6%. Copper is down 0.8% and gold is up 0.3% at $3,896.

The live gauge reads +1, which is mixed. Equities above their 200-day averages, a calm VIX at 18.4 and 9 of 14 indices up pull it toward risk on, but Thursday's 12bp jump in US yields and copper lagging gold cancel that out.
The 14:30 US PPI is the next test of the Fed-hike repricing. If yields extend, the dollar and rates keep the tone; if not, Europe's resilience can carry into the US open.
